svg.title: What share of income goes to households who spend as they earn?
svg.desc: Instrumental-variables estimates of lambda, the share of income going to hand-to-mouth households: Campbell and Mankiw's published values for 1953 to 1986 with 95 per cent intervals (the shaded band is the range of their Table 1 estimates, 0.351 to 0.698), and ours on US non-durables and services for their window, 1953 to 1986, for 1953 to 2019 and for 1953 to 2026, plus total spending for 1953 to 2019, each with its 95 per cent interval (solid) and its weak-instrument-robust Anderson-Rubin set (dashed, below). Open markers: effective F (Montiel Olea and Pflueger) of 10 or less. Educational demos made to show an open-source tool. Not research.

g.text: What share of income goes to households who spend as they earn?

text.style: fill: #57606a; font: 11px 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; text-anchor: start

g.text: US quarterly data per person: real non-durables + services (Fisher-chained), real disposable income (BEA, release of 30 Sep 2026). Theirs: the same concept, 1982 dollars.

text.style: fill: #57606a; font: 9.5px 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Arial', 'Helvetica', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; text-anchor: start

g.text: Educational demos made to show an open-source tool. Not research. Campbell and Mankiw (1989), Table 1, p. 192; ours: HAC (Newey-West, 4 lags); Anderson and Rubin (1949); Montiel Olea and Pflueger (2013).
